what: A cell line (MCF7, from ATCC) is recorded as kind `population`: it is a biological material with an identifier (RRID:CVCL_0031, Cellosaurus), and needs authentication and mycoplasma status, which the source does not report and the format cannot ask for.
need: biological materials as definition kinds; authentication
v0.39: resolved: kind `biological_material` with cellosaurus:CVCL_0031; authentication is for the wet-lab extension

what: Reagents (SMARTpool and single siRNAs with Dharmacon IDs such as D-001300-01; antibodies BD 610052, Sigma V-9131, …) have no place: identifiers of reagents fit `identifiers` only as CURIEs (RRID), and these have none in the source.
need: reagents with catalogue numbers and validation

what: Replicate structure (duplicate wells, two independent experiments per knockdown, 7-23 cells) is text. `n` would be either cells or experiments, and the two mean very different things for inference.
v0.39: extension: wet-lab (a third extension needing replicate structure would move it to the core)

what: Knockdown efficiency was confirmed by Western blot (Supplementary Fig S1); blots are specimens shown as figures. No way to say a figure is a blot, which lanes, or whether uncropped originals exist.
A 569-gene screen's per-gene results (D, p for each knockdown) is a large table I did not encode; the format can hold it as an artefact-backed table but the source gives no data file.

Genes are named in text (TPM1, RAC2). The knockdown is the intervention; the gene itself (HGNC/NCBI Gene ID) has no kind and is not a separate term, so a search for claims about RAC2 across papers depends on text.
need: genes and proteins as definition kinds
v0.39: resolved: the four genes are definitions of kind `entity` (D13-D16); HGNC identifiers left out, as the source gives none and this conversion did not look them up

what: A table whose rows are the four knockdowns plus the mock control needed a second group (D12) only because the control is not a member of the candidates group: rule 66 ties row labels to one dimension. Comparators in tables are routine in wet-lab work.
need: a control row in a table without an artificial group
proposal: core (allow the comparator as a row of a dimension's table)
v0.39: resolved: the mock control labels a row of the candidates' dimension; the artificial group is gone

what: The negative finding (TPM1 knockdown did not change forces) had to be dropped from the claim to avoid a compound statement; as its own claim it would need a null result with no test.
Causal claims from knockdowns in one cell line: fine as `causal` with scope. Mechanism ('slows force turnover') has no structure beyond text; acceptable.

The 0.38 conversion left TPM1's half-time empty and gave the others without saying they are approximate; the paper states 'about 1.5-fold' and 'roughly doubled'. The format has no way to mark a value as approximate, so the column's name says it.
proposal: open: core candidate (an `approximate` flag on a value, or guidance to record the stated number with uncertainty `unspecified`)

what: The genes are now definitions, but nothing links a knockdown (intervention D7) to the gene it targets (entity D13): a search for claims about RAC2 finds the definition, not the claims about knocking it down, unless they mention it.
proposal: open: core candidate (`targets` on an intervention, like `measures` on a variable)
